title: We Love This Outward World
description: We Love This Outward World in Tonic Solfa to ST. BRIDE, doh is Bb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 339, “The Meaning of Sorrow”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Short Metre (6.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. BRIDE; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: We love this out-ward world, Its fair sky o-ver-head, Its morn-ing's soft, gray mist un-furled, Its sun-sets rich and red.

lines: Its morning's soft, gray mist unfurled,
A life the immortal soul must win, —
The life of joy and faith.
Doth shade the world of sense,
The bounding play of health remove,
That, though the earth grows dull
The spirit gain its wisdom full
The world of victory o'er sin,
Of faith, and love, and light.

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1848.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to ST. BRIDE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
